citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518

isBasedOn.name: Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering

abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.

value: The ladder exists because a null is more useful when its location is known.
The descriptive composition rung never stops the ladder, which is why five of the six carry a pass rule.

additionalProperty.name: supporting_quote
additionalProperty.value: A null is more useful when its location is known. Six rungs, read in order, report the first link not demonstrated among the five that carry a pass rule: collapse, the oracle premise, whether the weights tracked reliability on held-out keyed items, measured by a Spearman correlation (Spearman 1904) whose 95 percent lower bound must exceed 0. 3, whether the weights improved the validity of what the pool accepted, a descriptive composition rung that never stops the ladder, and retention itself. A failed rung means a link was not demonstrated, not that the effect is absent.
